what: Nebius runs an artificial intelligence cloud. It builds and operates data centres full of graphics processors and rents that computing capacity to companies training and running AI models. It emerged from the restructuring of the Russian internet company Yandex.
customers: AI companies, model developers and enterprises needing large-scale GPU computing.
money: GPU compute capacity, storage and AI platform software
Avride self-driving, Toloka data labelling and an education business
moat: Data centre capacity and GPU supply secured ahead of demand, with its own software stack built by engineers who ran one of the largest search infrastructures in Europe.
risks: Debt of about $16 billion raised to fund data centre construction
It makes an operating loss while building capacity
Revenue is concentrated in a small number of very large contracts
GPU hardware depreciates quickly and may be worth far less in a few years
opportunities: Revenue grew nearly fivefold last year
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Demand for AI compute has exceeded supply, which supports pricing
watch: Contracted capacity, annualised run-rate revenue, and how new data centres are financed.
